questions.prompt: Where was the final part of the story displayed?

stimulus.title: The Story Trail
stimulus.body:
At a spring festival in a Victorian town, Leila helped set up a story trail. Each part appeared in a different shop window, with the ending at the library. The baker had fixed her page high to keep passing hands off the paper. Leila drew a route map for the first window. It had arrows showing the turns, but she left off the names of the stops.

Before the festival opened, Leila walked the trail with her grandfather. He paused at the bakery, looking up at the page above his eyes. Leila moved it lower, then stepped back to check whether the words could be read.

By lunchtime, several visitors had reached the library. Others returned to the first window to ask where the story finished. Leila replaced the map with a new one that named 'Library' beside the last arrow. She asked each shop to add the same note near its page.

Later, one visitor said the trail was easier to follow. Leila kept both maps, but did not write 'problem solved' on her report. By then the streets were quieter, and she had heard from only one visitor.

options.text: At the first window
At the library
At the bakery
At each shop

questions.explanation: The opening paragraph states that the story had its ending at the library. The reader must locate this detail and distinguish the final location from other places along the trail.

options.text: To explain why Leila needed to replace the route map
